topicName: Dimension Tables: SCD Types (Type 0 through Type 6)
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Dimension Tables: SCD Types (Type 0 through Type 6)"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to Slowly Changing Dimensions"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"In data warehousing, a Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) is a dimension that stores and manages data that changes slowly over time, rather than changing on a time-schedule or constant basis. Choosing the correct SCD type is crucial for maintaining historical accuracy while enabling proper analytical reporting."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"SCD Type 0: Retain Original"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"Type 0 never updates the dimension attributes. The data is fixed at the time of the initial insertion. This approach is used for attributes that should never change, such as a customer's original date of birth or initial sign-up location."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"SCD Type 1: Overwrite"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Type 1 overwrites the existing data with new data. No history is kept. This is useful for correcting typographical errors, but it destroys historical context for the changed attribute."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"UPDATE DimCustomer SET CustomerAddress = '123 New St' WHERE CustomerKey = 105;"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"SCD Type 2: Add New Row"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Type 2 is the most common approach for tracking history. When an attribute changes, a new row is inserted into the dimension table, and the old row is expired using effective and expiration dates, or a current flag."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"UPDATE DimCustomer SET IsCurrent = 0, ExpirationDate = '2023-10-01' WHERE CustomerId = 5 AND IsCurrent = 1; INSERT INTO DimCustomer (CustomerId, CustomerAddress, EffectiveDate, IsCurrent) VALUES (5, '123 New St', '2023-10-01', 1);"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"SCD Type 3: Add New Column"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Type 3 tracks changes by adding a new column to store the previous value alongside the current value. This approach is limited because it typically only preserves the single most recent historical change."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"UPDATE DimCustomer SET PreviousAddress = CurrentAddress, CurrentAddress = '123 New St' WHERE CustomerId = 5;"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"SCD Type 4: Add Mini-Dimension"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Type 4 involves separating rapidly changing attributes of a large dimension into a separate mini-dimension table. This prevents the primary dimension table from growing too large and isolates frequent changes."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"SCD Types 6: Hybrid Approach (Types 1 + 2 + 3)"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Often referred to as a hybrid approach, Type 6 combines Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3 techniques. It uses Type 2 row versioning, includes a Type 1 column to always show the current value across all historical rows, and a Type 3 column to show the prior value."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Type 0: No changes allowed."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Type 1: Overwrites current data."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Type 2: Creates new rows for history."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Type 3: Adds columns for previous values."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Type 6: Combines Type 1, 2, and 3 methodologies."}]
